title: Round 16 state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: Identity-safe verified rows added to California and the all-GNIS starter registers for Nevada and Arizona. California rows that remain VERIFIED=0 retain their public-source notes in resources/city-subsurface/cities.json and are not repeated as GNIS evidence here.

gnisMapServer.use: Exact-name / per-ID checks with outSR=4326. For a cited geometry row, the stored coordinate is one returned EPSG:4326 point as described in the row note—not a boundary, shoreline, peak polygon, or stream line.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature. Similar names and divisions were rejected explicitly where relevant.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Per-ID identity confirmation (official name, feature class, primary state/county) and coordinate sequence 1 for active hydrographic records that the current cartographic hydro layers did not return during the 2026-10-22 check.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service.

A stored multipoint coordinate is disclosed as one point. It is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, canyon outline, or stream centerline.
If the current GNIS class coverage omits the intended cultural feature, or a same-name record denotes a different feature, the curated row remains VERIFIED=0 with GNIS null.
No coordinate was copied from the non-reproducible js/socal-gazetteer-data.js snapshot for this round; that file was background only.

knownLimitations: Nevada and Arizona are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.
The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; the exact-match screening above is part of the evidence, and every accepted row names the returned type/county in cities.json.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain. Nevada and Arizona, like California, use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context corridors.
State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks.
